representation: Report-text-redacted structured guidelines, not the verbatim inference prompt

principles.instruction: Do not annotate an ANAT term when it solely names the body region or structure targeted by a recommended, follow-up, or additional imaging examination; annotate it only when it independently describes the location or anatomy of a report assessment.
principles.applies_when: An anatomical term occurs as part of the name, field, or coverage of a recommended imaging study, such as a CT, radiograph, or follow-up examination.
exceptions: Annotate anatomy in the same recommendation when it independently localizes or describes an assessed finding rather than merely specifying the imaging study target.
Anatomy in a directly stated finding or conclusion remains eligible, including when the finding is repeated.

principles.instruction: Use ANAT for anatomical structures, body regions, compartments, tissue types, and anatomical localization components.
principles.applies_when: A token or phrase component denotes where a finding is located or the bodily structure being described.
exceptions: Do not use ANAT for a device, surgical procedure, device feature, or finding merely because it is adjacent to anatomy.
A word with a non-anatomical role is not ANAT even if it can occur in anatomical expressions.

principles.instruction: Split composite anatomical expressions into their separately meaningful lexical components rather than creating one maximal anatomy span.
principles.applies_when: A multiword location contains laterality, orientation, level, region, structure, or tissue words.
exceptions: Keep a lexical unit intact when its measurement or observation descriptor is conventionally expressed as one unit.
Do not create entities for intervening function words, conjunctions, articles, or punctuation solely to bridge components.

principles.instruction: Use OBS-DP for a definitely asserted observation, whether abnormal, normal, stable, postoperative, or device-related.
principles.applies_when: The report directly states or affirms an imaging finding, morphology, measurement, quantity, change, normality, position, device, or procedure-related result.
exceptions: Do not assign OBS-DP merely because a word is medically salient; use OBS-U when the finding is explicitly hedged and OBS-DA when directly denied.
A body-structure word remains ANAT even when the associated observation is OBS-DP.

principles.instruction: Use OBS-DA for the finding target explicitly placed under definite negation or exclusion.
principles.applies_when: A direct negative construction denies a finding, pathology, abnormality, or clinically meaningful qualifier.
exceptions: Retain ANAT for the anatomical site within a negative statement.
Do not label negation cue words, absence verbs, or generic syntax by themselves.

In negative-evidence constructions, the directly denied evidence/target is OBS-DA; an embedded descriptive phrase may remain OBS-DP if it is analyzed as the described observation rather than the direct negated target.

principles.instruction: Use OBS-U only for a diagnostic, etiologic, or significance component that is explicitly placed under uncertainty scope. Keep OBS-DP for a directly asserted observed morphology, structural relationship, or uncertainty-status descriptor, and for unhedged finding names presented as alternatives in an [example omitted] differential.
principles.applies_when: An observation phrase contains uncertainty language, an artifact explanation, an indeterminate descriptor, or a differential alternative.
exceptions: A candidate diagnosis or etiology explicitly governed by wording such as [example omitted] [example omitted] [example omitted] or [example omitted] remains OBS-U.
Do not propagate uncertainty from a candidate interpretation or artifact explanation to a separately stated observed feature.
Anatomical structures remain ANAT regardless of the certainty assigned to associated observations.

principles.instruction: When adjacent lexical components independently express an observation or clinically meaningful observation characteristic, annotate them as separate entities rather than merging them into one maximal OBS-DP span, even when they have the same label.
principles.applies_when: An asserted finding phrase contains a modifier plus a head where each component has its own clinical meaning, such as a change descriptor plus a size descriptor or a postoperative/procedural descriptor plus surgical material.
exceptions: Keep a conventional inseparable lexical unit as one span when its components do not independently express distinct findings or characteristics.
Do not split punctuation, function words, or purely grammatical modifiers into entities.

principles.instruction: Annotate OBS-DP only for lexical components that directly express a finding or a clinically meaningful characteristic of a finding; do not annotate tokens whose sole role is to introduce, refer to, emphasize, temporally frame, measure-introduce, or specify the acquisition view/projection of another observation.
principles.applies_when: A candidate OBS-DP token occurs within a finding statement but functions only as discourse/anaphoric wording, a generic reporting noun, an emphasis or locative frame, a measurement-introducing verb, a temporal-comparison frame, or image-view/projection context.
exceptions: Annotate the substantive finding descriptor, morphology, change term, or complete numeric measurement that the contextual token frames.
Retain an image-view or projection term only when it independently states a clinically meaningful imaging finding rather than how another finding was visualized.

principles.instruction: Resolve context-sensitive words by their role in the current phrase, not by a fixed lexicon.
principles.applies_when: A term can denote anatomy in one context and an observation, device feature, or descriptor in another.
exceptions: Anatomical size, contour, or silhouette components are ANAT when they identify a body structure or structural attribute.
Size, shape, level, tip, centrality, or distal position is OBS-DP when it describes a lesion, device, or finding rather than anatomy.

principles.instruction: Before emitting any entity span, trim all immediately trailing non-lexical clause or sentence punctuation (including periods, commas, semicolons, and colons) so the exclusive end offset is the final character of the annotated lexical text.
principles.applies_when: An entity candidate of any label is immediately followed by punctuation in the source text.
exceptions: Retain punctuation only when it is an intrinsic, inseparable character of the annotated source token.
Do not trim internal punctuation that occurs within the lexical entity.

principles.instruction: For an explicitly asserted normality assessment expressed as [example omitted] annotate each lexical normality component—[example omitted] [example omitted] and [example omitted]—as a separate OBS-DP span.
principles.applies_when: A finding or anatomical structure is stated to be within normal limits in a diagnostic finding or conclusion section.
exceptions: Do not include surrounding anatomy, determiners, copulas, or punctuation in these OBS-DP spans.
Do not apply this rule when the phrase is negated, hypothetical, or used outside report assessment content.

principles.instruction: Use OBS-U for a diagnosis, etiology, or disease term introduced by an interpretation phrase such as [example omitted] [example omitted] or [example omitted] because the phrase presents the term as an inferential imaging interpretation rather than a directly established finding.
principles.applies_when: A diagnostic or etiologic observation follows an interpretation phrase linking it to an imaging appearance or other finding.
exceptions: Do not apply this rule to the directly observed morphology or imaging appearance that supports the interpretation; label that component independently according to its own assertion.
Do not apply this rule when the diagnosis is separately directly asserted without interpretive qualification in the same occurrence.

principles.instruction: In an uncertainty assessment construction stating that a finding is of unknown or uncertain clinical significance, annotate only the lexical component [example omitted] as OBS-U; do not include the generic assessment head [example omitted] in that entity span.
principles.applies_when: The phrase [example omitted] is governed by an explicit indeterminacy cue such as [example omitted] [example omitted] or [example omitted]
exceptions: Do not apply when [example omitted] independently expresses a distinct clinical finding rather than serving as the generic head of an uncertainty-assessment phrase.
Apply terminal-punctuation trimming independently under the punctuation-boundary rule.
